title: A nontrivial smooth connected unipotent group over a perfect field contains a central additive subgroup
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] which is perfect: either $\operatorname{char}k=0$, or $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$ and every element of $k$ is a $p$-th power. Let $V$ be a smooth connected affine $k$-group scheme of finite type [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Assume that $V$ is unipotent, meaning that in a faithful finite-dimensional linear representation every geometric point is a unipotent matrix, that is, its difference from the identity matrix is nilpotent. Assume $V$ is nontrivial, meaning it is not isomorphic to the trivial $k$-group scheme $\operatorname{Spec}k$. Then there exist a smooth connected closed subgroup scheme $N\subseteq V$ [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup] and an isomorphism of $k$-group schemes $a:\mathbf G_a\xrightarrow{\sim}N$ [def-sc-gm-ga]. Moreover $N$ is central: for every commutative $k$-algebra $R$, every $n\in N(R)$ and $v\in V(R)$ satisfy $nv=vn$ in $V(R)$. No dimension bound on $V$ is imposed.

source.place: Corollary 14.55 and its proof, printed p.297, in positive characteristic; Proposition 14.32 proof, printed p.289, first paragraph (a central normal series with additive quotients contains a central copy of Ga in positive dimension), in characteristic zero. A group variety here is smooth; a nontrivial smooth connected group over a perfect field has positive dimension.

proof.text: Embed $V$ as a closed subgroup of $U_n$ by [lem-sfb-geometric-unipotence-unitriangular-embedding]. Pull back the filtration of [lem-sfb-unitriangular-coordinate-filtration] to $H_j=V\cap U^{(j)}$. These are closed subgroups, defined by the indicated matrix-coordinate equations. For $h\in H_j(R)$ and $v\in V(R)$, triviality of unitriangular conjugation on $p_{j+1}$ gives $p_{j+1}(vhv^{-1}h^{-1})=0$, hence $[v,h]\in H_{j+1}(R)$ by its stated kernel. Thus this is a central series ending at $1$.

source.place: 14.21 proof and 6.49, printed pp.284--285 and pp.136--137

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-nilpotent-connected-central-series] to this series. As $V\ne1$, its resulting smooth connected series has a last nontrivial term $C$. The commutator condition with the next term $1$ says $vc=cv$ over every $k$-algebra. In particular $C$ is commutative. Restricting the closed embedding from step 1 embeds $C$ into $U_n$.
If $\operatorname{char}k=0$, apply [lem-sfb-char-zero-commutative-unipotent-vector-group] to $C$. We obtain an isomorphism $b:\mathbf G_a^d\simeq C$; $d\geq1$ since otherwise $C=1$.

If $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$, choose $e\geq1$ with $p^e\geq n$. Every matrix of $C(R)$ is $I+T$ with $T^n=0$. In characteristic $p$, $(I+T)^{p^e}=I+T^{p^e}=I$ by the binomial formula, over every commutative $k$-algebra $R$. Thus $[p^e]_C=0$.

source.place: 14.55 proof, printed p.297; bounded exponent made explicit using the unitriangular embedding

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-bounded-exponent-reduced-p-kernel] to $C$, obtaining a nontrivial smooth connected commutative closed subgroup $K\subseteq C$ killed by $p$. Apply [lem-sfb-perfect-exponent-p-vector-group] to obtain $b:\mathbf G_a^d\simeq K$, where $d\geq1$ because $K\ne1$.

In either case, take the image $N$ of the first coordinate factor under $b$ and then its inclusion into $V$. Its coordinate ideal is given, under $b$, by $x_2=\cdots=x_d=0$, so it is a closed subgroup and $a:t\mapsto b(t,0,\ldots,0)$ is an isomorphism $\mathbf G_a\simeq N$. The affine line is smooth (a polynomial algebra has freely liftable coordinate) and connected (its coordinate ring is a domain), so $N$ is smooth and connected. Since $N\subseteq C$, step 2 gives the required equality $nv=vn$ over every $R$.
